title: Sprint Gardeners' Manual: Pruning Rules & Rapid Triage
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for sprint-level backlog pruning and intake triage for Console & Rollouts. Think of it as the gardener's manual: how we trim, stake, and graft features so the backlog stays healthy and we ship high impact things each sprint.

Audience:
- PMs and designers in Console & Rollouts
- Triage hosts (rotating each sprint)
- Eng reps who attend grooming and sprint-planning

High-level principles (short):
1) Ship less, deliver more: prefer tiny vertical slices with measurable customer outcomes.
2) Observable first: any change that affects routing/rollouts/alerts needs an observability plan before commit.
3) Cost vs latency tradeoffs must be explicit on cards that touch serving/runtime behavior.
4) Fast feedback > perfect spec: wireframe + prototype + one assumption test beats 20 pages of docs.

Gardener's rules (prioritization heuristics):
- Blooming (High priority): Ships in <3 sprints, removes a top-3 support pain, or unlocks enterprise deal. Add explicit OKR link.
- Pollination (Medium): Improves developer UX or reduces operational toil by measurable percentage but requires >3 sprints.
- Seedlings (Low): Nice-to-have UX polish, deferred to backlog refinement cycles unless paired with a fast experiment.
- Weeds (Discard or Icebox): Duplicate tickets, vague asks without user impact, or requests without owner.

Quick triage flow (to run in 30–45m slot):
1) Intake review (5m): Organizer reads the one-sentence problem + proposed outcome. If unclear -> send back to reporter with template.
2) Impact check (10m): Who benefits? (customers, SRE, CS) Add impact tags: revenue, reliability, observability, dev-ex.
3) Groom type (10m): Mark as Feature | Bug | Infra | Spike. If Spike -> add explicit exit criteria.
4) Effort sense (5m): T-shirt size (S/M/L/XL) + a quick dependency callout.
5) Prioritize (10m): Slot into Blooming/Pollination/Seedlings/Weeds. If Blooming -> assign to next MVP cutlist.

Triage heuristics checklist (copyable into Jira quick comment):
- Customer reported? (Y/N) — link ticket
- Repro steps present? (Y/N)
- Observable -> logs/metric added? (Y/N)
- Security or compliance? (Y/N)
- Requires infra changes? (Y/N)
- SLA/regression risk? (Y/N)

Sample Jira filters (for triage host):
- Newly created for console team: project = CONSOLE AND created >= -7d AND labels not in (triaged)
- High priority unassigned: project = CONSOLE AND priority >= Major AND assignee is EMPTY
- Spikes: project = CONSOLE AND issuetype = Spike AND status in (Open, "In Review")
(Replace project key with CONSOLE-TEAM-BOARD in actual board)

Sprint planning routine (30–45m pre-planning + 90m planning):
Pre-planning (30–45m) - run by triage host:
- Build candidate cutlist: pick up to 6 Blooming items (target 40–60% velocity coverage)
- Confirm owners and acceptance criteria, add wireframe links or prototype urls
- Note cross-team dependencies and escalation owners

Planning meeting (90m):
- Round 1: Quick read of cutlist and owners (20m)
- Round 2: Dev estimates and capacity check (30m)
- Round 3: Swap-ins/outs and finalize commit (20m)
- Blockers/risks and rollout plan (20m)

Cutlist creation rules (how we choose the 6):
- At least one reliability or observability item per sprint unless on a stability freeze.
- No more than 2 items requiring major infra changes/ops pages.
- Include at least one small customer-visible quick win (<= 2 dev days).
- Reserve 10–15% buffer for bugs/urgent rollouts.

Wireframe notes (backlog view improvements):
- Show triage status chips inline: Blooming / Pollination / Seedling / Weed (color-coded).
- Add a mini-metrics column: recent support count, estimated cost impact, and last customer mention date.
- Quick actions on hover: "mark triaged", "request more info", "attach prototype".
- Keyboard-first grooming mode: j/k nav, space to expand, t to tag, c to comment. (Prototype: github.com/redwood/console-prototypes/ux-grooming-mode)
- Accessibility: ensure chips have text labels and high-contrast colors — asked SRE/design to add a11y audit ticket.

Observation experiments (small tests to validate rules):
- Experiment A (2 sprints): Force at least 1 Spike per sprint to reduce future unknowns. Measure # of blocked features reduced.
- Experiment B (1 sprint): Swap triage host to be an eng+pm pair. Measure decision velocity and re-open rate.

Decision log (quick):
- 2026-07-15: We will display triage tag in backlog list (agreed), design to provide color tokens by Aug 1. (owner: Lina)
- 2026-08-03: Adopt "gardener" metaphor for internal comms; not customer-facing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a compact customer-impact rubric (quantify support volume -> revenue bucket). Action: Priya to draft mapping with CS.
- Wireframe: how much horizontal real-estate for metrics? Design to iterate on 3 variations.
- Integrate cutlist with Releases page so release notes can be auto-populated. Who owns the linkage? Product-ops?

Notes to self (informal):
- If card is > XL, convert to an epic and add a 2-week discovery milestone.
- Push for test-deployment checkbox on any rollout card (must have a canary plan).

Appendix: grooming templates (copy into Jira comment)
- One-line problem statement:
  "Customer X is blocked by Y which causes Z (impact)."
- Proposed short outcome (how we know success):
  "Serve versioned route with A/B fallback; reduce support tickets by N/month."
- Exit criteria for Spikes:
  "Deliver prototype or doc with 3 success metrics and migration/residual work list."

Slack shorthand for triage questions:
- @triage-bot assign me if triage-needed CON-1234
- use #console-triage for fast async calls, prefix with [TRIAGE] in subject

Bottom line: we need consistent small decisions, visible outcomes, and fewer partial specs. This doc is intentionally light — it's a toolkit for the rotating groomers. Feedback welcome; will iterate into a more formal playbook after 3 sprints of usage.

-- Priya
